title: Compulsory Mathematics: Unit-wise Objective Question Bank

toc.title: 5.8 Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple

html:
The SEE Compulsory Mathematics paper has no multiple-choice group. Its 16 questions are built from items worth 1 mark upward, and the first items of most questions test knowledge: a formula, a definition, a one-line value. This chapter drills those objective items chapter by chapter, in multiple-choice form so that you can check each one in seconds. Each section opens with a facts line, gives six items, and ends with a key that has a one-line reason for every answer.

How to use the objective bank

These items are the 12 knowledge marks and some of the 18 understanding marks of the grid. They look easy, and the examiner means them to be; the risk is a slip in a formula or a unit. Work each item in under a minute, then read the reason. Take \pi=\frac{22}{7} unless an item says otherwise.

Practice items, not past questions

Every item is an original practice item written to the CDC pattern. None is claimed to have appeared in a particular year's paper. The numbers have been recomputed with a program as well as by hand.

5.1 Sets

Facts. n(A\cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A\cap B); (A\cup B)'=A'\cap B'; (A\cap B)'=A'\cup B'; n(U)=n(A\cup B)+n(A\cup B)'.

  1. If n(A)=20, n(B)=15 and n(A\cap B)=5, then n(A\cup B) is [1]a40b35c30d25
  2. If n(U)=50 and n(A\cup B)=40, then n(A\cup B)' is [1]a10b90c40d20
  3. (A\cup B)' equals [1]aA'\cup B'bA'\cap B'cA\cap BdA\cup B'
  4. If n(A)=25 and n(A\cap B)=8, the number of elements only in A is [1]a33b25c8d17
  5. In a class of 40, every student likes football or cricket; 25 like football and 20 like cricket. The number liking both is [1]a5b10c15d45
  6. If A\subset B, then A\cap B equals [1]aBb\emptysetcAdA\cup B
Answers

1. (c) — 20+15-5=30.

2. (a) — 50-40=10.

3. (b) — De Morgan's law.

4. (d) — 25-8=17.

5. (a) — 25+20-40=5.

6. (c) — every element of A is already in B.

5.2 Tax and Money Exchange

Facts. VAT at 13%: bill = price \times1.13. With excise duty e\% and VAT: price \times(1+\frac{e}{100})\times1.13. Currency: amount in one currency = amount in the other \times rate.

  1. VAT at 13% on a price of Rs 2000 is [1]aRs 13bRs 26cRs 130dRs 260
  2. A bill is Rs 11,300 including 13% VAT. The price without VAT is [1]aRs 9,830bRs 10,000cRs 11,287dRs 12,769
  3. A shopkeeper sells goods worth Rs 8000 plus 13% VAT. The bill is [1]aRs 8,013bRs 8,104cRs 9,040dRs 8,130
  4. If USD 1 = Rs 130, USD 200 is [1]aRs 650bRs 2,600cRs 13,000dRs 26,000
  5. If Rs 160 = INR 100, then INR 5000 is [1]aRs 3,125bRs 8,000cRs 80,000dRs 5,160
  6. A factory price of Rs 1000 carries 10% excise duty and then 13% VAT. The final price is [1]aRs 1,230bRs 1,243cRs 1,243.30dRs 1,100
Answers

1. (d) — 0.13\times2000=260.

2. (b) — 11300\div1.13=10000.

3. (c) — 8000\times1.13=9040.

4. (d) — 200\times130=26000.

5. (b) — 5000\times\frac{160}{100}=8000.

6. (b) — 1000\times1.10\times1.13=1243; VAT applies to price plus excise.

5.3 Compound Interest

Facts. A=P\left(1+\frac{R}{100}\right)^{T}; CI=A-P; half-yearly: A=P\left(1+\frac{R}{200}\right)^{2T}. For 2 years, CI-SI=P\left(\frac{R}{100}\right)^{2}.

  1. The amount on Rs 10,000 for 2 years at 10% compound interest per annum is [1]aRs 12,000bRs 12,100cRs 12,200dRs 2,100
  2. The compound interest in item 1 is [1]aRs 2,000bRs 2,100cRs 12,100dRs 1,000
  3. Rs 4000 at 10% p.a. compounded half-yearly for 1 year amounts to [1]aRs 4,400bRs 4,410cRs 4,420dRs 4,200
  4. For Rs 8000 at 5% for 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is [1]aRs 8bRs 20cRs 40dRs 800
  5. A principal becomes Rs 1331 in 3 years at 10% compound interest. The principal is [1]aRs 1,000bRs 1,100cRs 900dRs 1,210
  6. In half-yearly compounding the rate used per period is [1]aRb2Rc\frac{R}{2}d\frac{R}{4}
Answers

1. (b) — 10000(1.1)^2=12100.

2. (b) — 12100-10000=2100.

3. (b) — rate per half-year 5%, two periods: 4000(1.05)^2=4410.

4. (b) — 8000\times(0.05)^2=20.

5. (a) — 1331\div(1.1)^3=1331\div1.331=1000.

6. (c) — the annual rate is halved and the periods doubled.

5.4 Population Growth and Depreciation

Facts. Growth: P_T=P_0\left(1+\frac{R}{100}\right)^{T}. Depreciation: V_T=V_0\left(1-\frac{R}{100}\right)^{T}. Net rate of growth = birth rate - death rate \pm net migration rate.

  1. A population of 20,000 grows at 5% a year. After 2 years it is [1]a22,000b22,050c22,500d21,000
  2. A population of 5000 decreases by 10% a year. After 2 years it is [1]a4,000b4,050c4,500d3,500
  3. A town has 24,200 people now; the growth rate is 10% a year. Two years ago it had [1]a20,000b19,360c21,000d22,000
  4. A machine of value Rs 80,000 depreciates 10% a year. After 2 years its value is [1]aRs 64,000bRs 64,800cRs 72,000dRs 60,000
  5. Birth rate 3%, death rate 1% and out-migration 0.5% give a net growth rate of [1]a1.5%b2%c2.5%d4.5%
  6. A quantity of 1000 grows 10% in year 1 and 20% in year 2. At the end it is [1]a1,300b1,320c1,330d1,440
Answers

1. (b) — 20000(1.05)^2=22050.

2. (b) — 5000(0.9)^2=4050.

3. (a) — 24200\div(1.1)^2=20000.

4. (b) — 80000(0.9)^2=64800.

5. (a) — 3-1-0.5=1.5.

6. (b) — 1000\times1.1\times1.2=1320.

5.5 Plane Surfaces

Facts. Heron: A=\sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} with s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}; circle A=\pi r^2, C=2\pi r; ring A=\pi(R^2-r^2); sector A=\frac{\theta}{360}\pi r^2.

  1. The area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is [1]a84 cm²b90 cm²c168 cm²d42 cm²
  2. A ring has outer radius 14 cm and inner radius 7 cm. Its area is [1]a154 cm²b308 cm²c462 cm²d616 cm²
  3. A path 1 m wide runs around the outside of a 20 m × 15 m garden. The area of the path is [1]a70 m²b74 m²c72 m²d76 m²
  4. The number of 20 cm × 20 cm tiles needed for a 6 m × 4 m floor is [1]a60b120c600d6000
  5. The area of a quadrant (90° sector) of radius 14 cm is [1]a154 cm²b308 cm²c616 cm²d77 cm²
  6. The perimeter of a semicircle of diameter 14 cm is [1]a22 cmb36 cmc44 cmd58 cm
Answers

1. (a) — s=21; \sqrt{21\times8\times7\times6}=\sqrt{7056}=84.

2. (c) — \frac{22}{7}(196-49)=\frac{22}{7}\times147=462.

3. (b) — outer 22\times17=374; inner 20\times15=300; 374-300=74.

4. (c) — area 24 m² over 0.04 m² per tile gives 600.

5. (a) — \frac14\times\frac{22}{7}\times196=154.

6. (b) — arc \frac{22}{7}\times7=22, plus diameter 14, gives 36.

5.6 Cylinder and Sphere

Facts. Cylinder: curved surface area 2\pi rh, total 2\pi r(r+h), volume \pi r^2h. Sphere: surface area 4\pi r^2, volume \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3. Hemisphere: curved 2\pi r^2, total 3\pi r^2, volume \frac{2}{3}\pi r^3. 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

  1. The curved surface area of a cylinder with r=7 cm and h=10 cm is [1]a220 cm²b440 cm²c1540 cm²d308 cm²
  2. The volume of the same cylinder is [1]a440 cm³b770 cm³c1540 cm³d3080 cm³
  3. The surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm is [1]a154 cm²b308 cm²c616 cm²d1437 cm²
  4. The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm is [1]a308 cm²b462 cm²c616 cm²d154 cm²
  5. The volume of a sphere of radius 10.5 cm is [1]a2425 cm³b4851 cm³c4620 cm³d1617 cm³
  6. A cylindrical tank has radius 0.7 m and height 2 m. Its capacity is [1]a308 litresb1540 litresc3080 litresd30 800 litres
Answers

1. (b) — 2\times\frac{22}{7}\times7\times10=440.

2. (c) — \frac{22}{7}\times49\times10=1540.

3. (c) — 4\times\frac{22}{7}\times49=616.

4. (b) — 3\pi r^2=3\times\frac{22}{7}\times49=462.

5. (b) — \frac43\times\frac{22}{7}\times(10.5)^3=4851.

6. (c) — \frac{22}{7}\times0.49\times2=3.08 m³ =3080 litres.

5.7 Prism and Pyramid

Facts. Prism: volume = base area \times height (length); lateral surface area = perimeter of base \times height; total = lateral +\ 2\times base area. Square pyramid: volume =\frac{1}{3}\times base area \times height; lateral area =\frac{1}{2}\times perimeter \times slant height; l^2=h^2+\left(\frac{b}{2}\right)^2. 1 m³ = 1000 litres.

  1. A triangular prism has a base area of 6 cm² and length 10 cm. Its volume is [1]a16 cm³b30 cm³c60 cm³d120 cm³
  2. A right triangular prism has a base with sides 3 cm, 4 cm, 5 cm and length 10 cm. Its lateral surface area is [1]a60 cm²b120 cm²c132 cm²d12 cm²
  3. The total surface area of the prism in item 2 is [1]a120 cm²b126 cm²c132 cm²d144 cm²
  4. A square pyramid has base side 6 cm and height 4 cm. Its slant height is [1]a4 cmb5 cmc6 cmd7 cm
  5. The volume of the pyramid in item 4 is [1]a24 cm³b48 cm³c72 cm³d144 cm³
  6. The area of the four walls of a room 5 m × 4 m × 3 m is [1]a27 m²b54 m²c60 m²d94 m²
Answers

1. (c) — 6\times10=60.

2. (b) — perimeter 12\times10=120.

3. (c) — base area \frac12\times3\times4=6, so 120+2(6)=132.

4. (b) — l=\sqrt{4^2+3^2}=5.

5. (b) — \frac13\times36\times4=48.

6. (b) — 2(5+4)\times3=54.

5.8 Highest Common Factor and Lowest Common Multiple

Facts. Factorise completely first. HCF is the product of the common factors of least power; LCM is the product of all factors of greatest power. \text{HCF}\times\text{LCM}= product of the two expressions.

  1. The HCF of x^2-y^2 and x+y is [1]ax-ybx+ycx^2-y^2d1
  2. The LCM of 3x^2y and 6xy^2 is [1]a3xyb6xyc6x^2y^2d18x^3y^3
  3. The HCF of 12a^2b and 18ab^2 is [1]a36a^2b^2b6abc6a^2b^2d3ab
  4. The LCM of x^2-4 and x-2 is [1]ax-2bx+2cx^2-4d(x-2)^2
  5. The HCF of x^2+5x+6 and x^2+3x+2 is [1]ax+1bx+2cx+3dx-2
  6. If one expression is (x+2)(x-3), the HCF is x+2 and the LCM is (x+2)(x-3)(x+1), the other expression is [1]ax+1bx-3c(x+2)(x+1)d(x-3)(x+1)
Answers

1. (b) — x^2-y^2=(x-y)(x+y), so the common factor is x+y.

2. (c) — LCM of 3 and 6 is 6, and the highest powers are x^2 and y^2.

3. (b) — HCF of 12 and 18 is 6, lowest powers a and b.

4. (c) — x^2-4=(x-2)(x+2) already contains x-2.

5. (b) — (x+2)(x+3) and (x+1)(x+2) share x+2.

6. (c) — other =\frac{\text{HCF}\times\text{LCM}}{\text{given}}=\frac{(x+2)\cdot(x+2)(x-3)(x+1)}{(x+2)(x-3)}=(x+2)(x+1).

5.9 Radical and Surd

Facts. \sqrt{ab}=\sqrt{a}\sqrt{b}; the conjugate of a+\sqrt{b} is a-\sqrt{b} and (a+\sqrt{b})(a-\sqrt{b})=a^2-b. Rationalise by multiplying by the conjugate. If x+\frac1x=k then x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}=k^2-2.

  1. \sqrt{12} in simplest form is [1]a3\sqrt{2}b2\sqrt{3}c4\sqrt{3}d6
  2. \sqrt{18}+\sqrt{8} equals [1]a\sqrt{26}b5\sqrt{2}c6\sqrt{2}d13
  3. (2+\sqrt{3})(2-\sqrt{3}) equals [1]a1b7c4-\sqrt{3}d2
  4. The rationalised form of \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}-1} is [1]a\sqrt{3}-1b\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}c\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}d\sqrt{3}+1
  5. If x=2+\sqrt{3}, then \frac1x is [1]a2+\sqrt{3}b\sqrt{3}-2c2-\sqrt{3}d\frac{1}{2}
  6. If x=2+\sqrt{3}, then x^2+\frac{1}{x^2} equals [1]a4b14c16d18
Answers

1. (b) — \sqrt{4\times3}=2\sqrt{3}.

2. (b) — 3\sqrt{2}+2\sqrt{2}=5\sqrt{2}.

3. (a) — 4-3=1.

4. (b) — \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{(\sqrt{3})^2-1}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}.

5. (c) — (2+\sqrt{3})(2-\sqrt{3})=1, so the reciprocal is 2-\sqrt{3}.

6. (b) — x+\frac1x=4, so x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}=16-2=14.

5.10 Indices

Facts. a^m\times a^n=a^{m+n}; \frac{a^m}{a^n}=a^{m-n}; (a^m)^n=a^{mn}; a^0=1; a^{-n}=\frac{1}{a^n}; a^{\frac{m}{n}}=\sqrt[n]{a^m}. If a^x=a^y then x=y.

  1. 2^3\times2^4 equals [1]a2^{12}b4^7c2^7d2^{1}
  2. The value of 64^{\frac23} is [1]a4b8c16d32
  3. The value of 2^{-3} is [1]a-8b-6c\frac{1}{6}d\frac{1}{8}
  4. If 3^x=81, then x is [1]a3b4c27d5
  5. \frac{(x^2)^3}{x^4} equals [1]ax^2bx^3cx^{10}dx^{-2}
  6. The value of (25)^0+5^{-1}\times5 is [1]a1b2c5d6
Answers

1. (c) — add the powers: 2^{3+4}=2^7.

2. (c) — 64^{2/3}=(4^3)^{2/3}=4^2=16.

3. (d) — 2^{-3}=\frac{1}{2^3}.

4. (b) — 81=3^4.

5. (a) — \frac{x^6}{x^4}=x^2.

6. (b) — 1+\frac15\times5=1+1=2.

5.11 Algebraic Fraction

Facts. Factorise, then cancel common factors. Add or subtract over the LCM of the denominators. \frac ab\div\frac cd=\frac{ad}{bc}. The difference of squares: a^2-b^2=(a-b)(a+b).

  1. \frac{x^2-9}{x-3} simplifies to [1]ax-3bx+3cx^2-3d3
  2. \frac1x+\frac1y equals [1]a\frac{2}{x+y}b\frac{1}{xy}c\frac{x+y}{xy}d\frac{xy}{x+y}
  3. \frac{a}{b}\div\frac{c}{d} equals [1]a\frac{ac}{bd}b\frac{bc}{ad}c\frac{ad}{bc}d\frac{a}{bc}
  4. \frac{1}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x+1} equals [1]a0b\frac{2}{x^2-1}c\frac{2x}{x^2-1}d\frac{1}{x^2-1}
  5. \frac{x^2+3x+2}{x^2+x} simplifies to [1]a\frac{x+2}{x}b\frac{x+1}{x}c\frac{x+2}{x+1}d2
  6. \frac{2}{x}+\frac{3}{x} equals [1]a\frac{5}{2x}b\frac{6}{x^2}c\frac{5}{x}d\frac{5}{x^2}
Answers

1. (b) — \frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=x+3.

2. (c) — common denominator xy.

3. (c) — invert the divisor and multiply.

4. (b) — \frac{(x+1)-(x-1)}{x^2-1}=\frac{2}{x^2-1}.

5. (a) — \frac{(x+1)(x+2)}{x(x+1)}=\frac{x+2}{x}.

6. (c) — same denominator, add numerators.

5.12 Equations

Facts. Elimination or substitution for two linear equations. Quadratic by factorising or x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}. Check roots in the original problem and reject any that make no sense (such as a negative length).

  1. If x+y=7 and x-y=1, then x is [1]a3b4c5d6
  2. The roots of x^2-5x+6=0 are [1]a1 and 6b-2 and -3c2 and 3d-1 and -6
  3. The solutions of x^2=49 are [1]a7 onlyb\pm7c\pm 24.5d-7 only
  4. The equation x^2+2x+1=0 has [1]atwo distinct rootsbno real rootcone repeated root x=-1droot x=1
  5. Two numbers have sum 10 and difference 2. The larger is [1]a4b5c6d8
  6. The length of a rectangle is 3 m more than its breadth and its area is 40 m². The breadth is [1]a4 mb5 mc8 md10 m
Answers

1. (b) — adding gives 2x=8.

2. (c) — (x-2)(x-3)=0.

3. (b) — both 7 and -7 square to 49.

4. (c) — (x+1)^2=0.

5. (c) — a+b=10, a-b=2 gives a=6.

6. (b) — b(b+3)=40\Rightarrow(b+8)(b-5)=0; reject b=-8.

5.13 Area of Triangles and Quadrilaterals

Facts. Triangle =\frac12\times base \times height. Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area. A triangle and a parallelogram on the same base and between the same parallels: triangle =\frac12 parallelogram. A median divides a triangle into two triangles of equal area.

  1. The area of a triangle of base 10 cm and height 6 cm is [1]a16 cm²b30 cm²c60 cm²d36 cm²
  2. A triangle and a parallelogram stand on the same base and between the same parallels. If the parallelogram has area 40 cm², the triangle has area [1]a80 cm²b40 cm²c20 cm²d10 cm²
  3. A median divides a triangle of area 36 cm² into two triangles each of area [1]a9 cm²b12 cm²c18 cm²d36 cm²
  4. The area of a rhombus with diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm is [1]a240 cm²b120 cm²c34 cm²d60 cm²
  5. The area of a trapezium with parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm is [1]a40 cm²b50 cm²c100 cm²d60 cm²
  6. Parallelograms on the same base and between the same parallels are [1]acongruentbequal in areacsimilar onlydequal in perimeter
Answers

1. (b) — \frac12\times10\times6=30.

2. (c) — triangle is half the parallelogram.

3. (c) — a median bisects the area: 36\div2=18.

4. (b) — \frac12\times10\times24=120.

5. (b) — \frac12(8+12)\times5=50.

6. (b) — equal in area, though not necessarily congruent.

5.14 Construction

Facts. To construct a triangle equal in area to a quadrilateral, join a diagonal and draw a line through the opposite vertex parallel to that diagonal. Triangles on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in area. A rectangle equal to a triangle has the same base and half the height.

  1. The theorem used to construct a triangle equal in area to a given quadrilateral is [1]atriangles on the same base and between the same parallels are equal in areabangle in a semicircle is 90°cPythagoras' theoremdthe sine rule
  2. A rectangle equal in area to a triangle of base 8 cm and height 6 cm has the same base and a height of [1]a6 cmb12 cmc3 cmd4 cm
  3. A square equal in area to a rectangle of 9 cm × 4 cm has side [1]a5 cmb6 cmc6.5 cmd13 cm
  4. The area of a triangle with base 8 cm and height 6 cm is [1]a14 cm²b48 cm²c24 cm²d12 cm²
  5. To draw a line through a point parallel to a given line, you use [1]aequal alternate anglesbthe mediancthe centroiddthe perimeter
  6. In the steps of construction, the compass arcs [1]ashould be rubbed outbshould be left visiblecare not requireddare replaced by a ruler line
Answers

1. (a) — shifting the vertex along a parallel keeps the area.

2. (c) — triangle area 24 cm²; with base 8 cm the rectangle height is 24\div8=3 cm, half the triangle's height.

3. (b) — area 36, side 6 cm.

4. (c) — \frac12\times8\times6=24.

5. (a) — copy an angle so the alternate angles are equal.

6. (b) — examiners credit visible construction arcs.

5.15 Circle

Facts. Angle at the centre =2\times angle at the circumference on the same arc. Angles in the same segment are equal. Angle in a semicircle =90^\circ. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180^\circ. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact. A perpendicular from the centre bisects a chord.

  1. An arc subtends 40° at the circumference. The angle at the centre is [1]a20°b40°c80°d160°
  2. The angle in a semicircle is [1]a45°b90°c120°d180°
  3. One angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is 110°. The opposite angle is [1]a70°b110°c90°d250°
  4. A point is 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm. The length of a tangent from the point is [1]a8 cmb12 cmc18 cmd144 cm
  5. Angles in the same segment standing on one chord are [1]acomplementarybsupplementarycequalddouble
  6. A chord of length 16 cm lies in a circle of radius 10 cm. Its distance from the centre is [1]a4 cmb6 cmc8 cmd12 cm
Answers

1. (c) — the centre angle is twice: 2\times40=80.

2. (b) — a diameter subtends a right angle.

3. (a) — 180-110=70.

4. (b) — \sqrt{13^2-5^2}=\sqrt{144}=12.

5. (c) — equal angles in the same segment.

6. (b) — half-chord 8, so \sqrt{10^2-8^2}=6.

5.16 Trigonometry

Facts. \sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1; 1+\tan^2\theta=\sec^2\theta. \sin30^\circ=\frac12, \cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}, \tan45^\circ=1, \sin60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}. \sin\theta=\cos(90^\circ-\theta).

  1. The value of \sin30^\circ is [1]a\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}b1c\frac12d\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}
  2. If \sin\theta=\frac{5}{13} and \theta is acute, then \cos\theta is [1]a\frac{12}{13}b\frac{8}{13}c\frac{5}{12}d\frac{13}{12}
  3. \sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta equals [1]a0b\sin2\thetac\tan^2\thetad1
  4. \sin25^\circ equals [1]a\cos25^\circb\cos65^\circc\tan65^\circd\sin65^\circ
  5. The angle of elevation of a tower top from a point 20 m away is 45^\circ. The height of the tower is [1]a10 mb20 mc20\sqrt{2} md40 m
  6. The value of \sin^230^\circ+\cos^230^\circ is [1]a\frac12b\frac34c\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}d1
Answers

1. (c) — standard value.

2. (a) — hypotenuse 13, opposite 5, adjacent \sqrt{169-25}=12.

3. (d) — the basic identity.

4. (b) — complementary angles: \sin\theta=\cos(90^\circ-\theta).

5. (b) — \tan45^\circ=1=\frac{h}{20}, so h=20 m.

6. (d) — \frac14+\frac34=1.

5.17 Statistics

Facts. Range =L-S; coefficient of range =\frac{L-S}{L+S}. Quartile deviation =\frac{Q_3-Q_1}{2}; its coefficient is \frac{Q_3-Q_1}{Q_3+Q_1}. Standard deviation \sigma=\sqrt{\frac{\sum(x-\bar x)^2}{n}}. Coefficient of variation =\frac{\sigma}{\bar x}\times100\%; the smaller it is, the more consistent the data.

  1. The largest value is 48 and the smallest is 12. The range is [1]a30b36c60d4
  2. The coefficient of range in item 1 is [1]a0.6b0.4c0.75d1.6
  3. If Q_1=20 and Q_3=40, the quartile deviation is [1]a20b30c10d60
  4. The coefficient of quartile deviation for Q_1=20 and Q_3=40 is [1]a\frac12b\frac13c\frac23d20

Facts. P(E)=\frac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes}}; P(E')=1-P(E); P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B). Without replacement, the second draw has one fewer ball.
